{{Short description|Review of systematic reviews or meta-analyses}}
In [[Medicine|medical]] [[research]], an '''umbrella review''' is a review of [[systematic reviews]] or [[meta-analyses]].<ref name="Aromataris2015"/><ref name="Fusar-Poli2018"/><ref name="Brown2020"/> They may also be called overviews of reviews, reviews of reviews, summaries of systematic reviews, or syntheses of reviews.<ref name="Aromataris2015"/> Umbrella reviews are among the highest [[Hierarchy of evidence|levels of evidence]] currently available in medicine.<ref name="Fusar-Poli2018"/>

By summarizing information from multiple overview articles, umbrella reviews make it easier to review the evidence and allow for comparison of results between each of the individual reviews.<ref name="Aromataris2015"/> Umbrella reviews may address a broader question than a typical review, such as discussing multiple different treatment comparisons instead of only one.<ref name="Aromataris2015"/><ref name="Brown2020"/> They are especially useful for developing guidelines and clinical practice, and when comparing competing interventions.<ref name="Aromataris2015"/><ref name="Brown2020"/>
